> Bootstrap 5 components for htmxr — no CSS knowledge required.

**Documentation:** [hyperverse.world](https://hyperverse.world)

`{htmxr.bootstrap}` is an opinionated layer on top of [`{htmxr}`](https://github.com/hyperverse-r/htmxr).
It wraps each `{htmxr}` primitive with Bootstrap 5 classes applied automatically —
buttons, pages, inputs — so you get a polished UI without writing a single CSS class.

## Installation

```r
pak::pak("hyperverse-r/htmxr.bootstrap")
```

## Example — Hello, Bootstrap!

The `hello` example ships with `{htmxr.bootstrap}`. It shows a page with
Bootstrap buttons that trigger an htmx request and update the DOM.

### The page

`hx_bs_page()` builds a complete HTML page with Bootstrap CSS and JS already
injected. `hx_bs_button()` generates a `<button>` with the right Bootstrap
variant classes and htmx attributes.

```r
#* @get /
#* @parser none
#* @serializer html
function() {
  hx_bs_page(
    hx_head(title = "Hello, Bootstrap!"),
    tags$div(
      class = "container py-5",
      tags$h1(class = "mb-4", "Hello, Bootstrap!"),
      tags$p(class = "text-muted mb-4", "Click a button to greet the server."),
      tags$div(
        class = "d-flex gap-2 mb-4",
        hx_bs_button(
          "Say hello",
          variant = "warning",
          get = "/greet",
          target = "#result",
          swap = "innerHTML"
        ),
        hx_bs_button(
          "Say hello (outline)",
          variant = "secondary",
          outline = TRUE,
          get = "/greet",
          target = "#result",
          swap = "innerHTML"
        ),
        hx_bs_button(
          "Say hello (primary)",
          variant = "primary",
          get = "/greet",
          target = "#result",
          swap = "innerHTML"
        ),
        hx_bs_button("Disabled", variant = "danger", disabled = TRUE)
      ),
      tags$div(id = "result", class = "alert alert-light border")
    )
  )
}
```

### The endpoint

```r
#* @get /greet
#* @parser none
#* @serializer none
function() {
  tags$span(paste("Hello from the server!", format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S")))
}
```

### Run it

```r
hx_bs_run_example("hello")
```

## Design philosophy

`{htmxr.bootstrap}` is built around a few explicit choices:

- **Opinionated by design** — Bootstrap classes are applied automatically.
  You pick a `variant`, a `size`, a state — the right classes follow.
  You never need to know that `"btn btn-outline-danger btn-sm"` is the correct string.

- **One function per component** — `hx_bs_button()`, `hx_bs_page()`, etc.
  map directly to Bootstrap components. No configuration objects, no theming system to learn.

- **Built on `{htmxr}`** — Every `hx_bs_*` function delegates to the corresponding
  `{htmxr}` primitive. All htmx attributes (`get`, `post`, `target`, `swap`, …) are
  passed through unchanged.

- **Bootstrap bundled locally** — Bootstrap 5.3.8 CSS and JS are included in the
  package under `inst/`. No CDN dependency at runtime.

- **Short aliases** — Every function has a `bs_*` alias (`bs_button`, `bs_page`, …)
  for users who prefer concise code.
